headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,500 as Iran-US Strikes Intensify; Experts Set $4,650-$4,750 June Range
snippet: Gold steadied above $4,500/oz on June 1 as renewed Iran-US military strikes intensified geopolitical safe-haven demand; a Reuters poll of 30 analysts puts the 2026 median forecast at $4,746, with one metals CEO setting the June base case at $4,650–$4,750 and the top of the range at $4,800.

headline: SILVER AT $75.53 — 3% Monthly Gain Sets Up Test of $81 Resistance as Year-Six Deficit Deepens
snippet: Silver closed May at $75.53/oz with a 3% monthly gain, entering its sixth consecutive year of supply deficit; combined visible inventories at COMEX, LBMA, and Shanghai have dropped nearly 1 billion ounces since 2021, and a break above $81 resistance would open the path toward $90.

headline: COPPER CLIMBS TO $6.43/lb: Chile's April Output Worst in 23 Years Deepens Structural Deficit
snippet: Copper futures rose 1.08% to $6.43/lb on June 1 — up 33% year-over-year — as Chile's April production fell 13.8% to 399,954 metric tonnes, the weakest monthly output in over two decades; AI data center buildout and grid electrification are amplifying demand against an already constrained supply picture.

headline: URANIUM HOLDS $83/lb as Meta and Microsoft Sign Nuclear Power Deals for AI Data Centers
snippet: Uranium spot steadied at $83.35/lb on June 1 — well below January's $101/lb speculative peak — as utility spot buying remains muted but Meta and Microsoft have signed new nuclear power agreements for AI data center load; a full U.S. ban on Russian enriched uranium takes effect in 2028, accelerating Western utility contracting.

headline: 27% CORRECTION NOW RESOLVING: Gold's June 2026 Technical Setup Points to $5,000 Q4 Target
snippet: The gold-silver correction from the intraday peak reached approximately 27% — comparable to prior major bull-market resets — before producing a technically significant 200-day moving average reversal signal; the correction appears in its late-stage resolution phase with key support at $4,184–$4,423 and $5,000/oz the Q4 2026 base case.

headline: MINERS BEATING THE METAL: $2,800/oz Margins and 40% Net Profit Signal a Long-Delayed Re-Rating
snippet: With industry-wide AISC below $2,500/oz and gold near $4,500+, gold miners are generating $2,800/oz margins and 40% net profit — rivaling big tech's profitability; institutional funds are beginning a sectoral re-weighting into mining equities that analysts argue is only just starting, with junior explorers the high-leverage play.

headline: CHINA RAISES RARE EARTH PRICES 45% IN ONE QUARTER — Seventh Straight Hike Shakes Western Supply Chains
snippet: China Northern Rare Earth Group set Q2 2026 concentrate at 38,804 yuan/tonne — a 45% quarterly jump and the largest single-quarter increase since 2023's pricing reform — marking the seventh consecutive quarterly hike; European rare earth prices have reached up to six times Chinese domestic levels as export licensing approvals for Western firms fell below 25% in some sectors.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE BOOM Lifts Beaten-Down Lithium: Storage Demand to Hit 31% of Market in 2026
snippet: A boom in grid-scale battery storage has materially strengthened the demand outlook for lithium; Guotai Junan projects energy storage will account for 31% of total lithium carbonate equivalent demand in 2026, up from 23% in 2025 — the clearest path yet to absorbing the sector's multi-year oversupply overhang and supporting a price floor.

headline: MINING M&A HITS $21.6B IN Q1 2026: 121 Deals as Critical Minerals Drive Fastest Consolidation Wave in a Decade
snippet: The first quarter of 2026 recorded 121 mining transactions totaling $21.6 billion — up from 117 deals and $16.1 billion in Q1 2025 — as critical minerals supply-chain security drives deal activity; strategic partnerships are the preferred structure, with North American projects capturing 66% of total capital announced.

headline: BUNKER HILL MINE 93% READY: Idaho Silver Restart Imminent as Cate-8 High-Grade Zone Returns Visible Galena
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining's historic Idaho silver-lead-zinc mine is 93% through pre-production commissioning — mills turning, filter plant 100% mechanically complete, and stockpiles sufficient for three months of operations — with a June restart on track; first Cate-8 underground drill hole returned 52.3 feet of continuous visible galena, the first new high-grade silver target developed ahead of first production.

headline: HYCROFT MINING JOINS RUSSELL 3000 June 29 — Nevada Gold-Silver Developer Added to Broad Market Index
snippet: Hycroft Mining, owner of one of the largest undeveloped gold-silver deposits in the U.S. at its Nevada mine, will join the Russell 3000 Index effective June 29, 2026; the inclusion brings mandatory passive-fund buying and signals growing institutional recognition of U.S.-listed precious metals developers as a distinct asset class.

headline: WHY SILVER IS OUTPERFORMING GOLD: Byproduct Mining, Solar Surge, and 1 Billion oz Inventory Drawdown
snippet: Money Metals details silver's structural supply ceiling: the metal is predominantly mined as a byproduct and producers cannot quickly scale output in response to demand spikes; China's solar production pushed imports above 790 tonnes in early 2026, while six consecutive years of deficits have erased nearly 1 billion ounces from combined global visible stocks.
